dimension_justifications.soundness: The finite-domain selector, boundary sets, NFE totals, cardinalities, and median-discreteness discussion are internally consistent, and the manuscript carefully avoids converting bootstrap stability into false-positive control. However, the event-time coordinate, final-value semantics, missing/terminal handling, and positionwise analyzed cohorts are unspecified. These choices are load-bearing because they determine whether lock times are comparable across blocks and can themselves create boundary discontinuities. All numerical evidence is source-reported, the probe argmaxes lack complete vectors, and registration claims cannot be audited.
dimension_justifications.presentation: The paper is unusually explicit about evidence tiers, composite treatment, post-treatment scope changes, single-locus support, and cannot-verify boundaries. Definitions and limitations are generally precise, anonymity is preserved, the main text fits the nine-page limit, and an AI-use disclosure is present. Evaluation is nevertheless obstructed by dense qualification, incomplete probe tables, and inconsistent emphasis on BIN8 versus the load-bearing BIN16 content null.
dimension_justifications.contribution: The paper offers a useful measurement warning and a precise recommendation to separate algebraic reachability from event-supported magnitude. Its empirical scope is narrow: one private checkpoint family, one task, a composite partition/allocation intervention, a reused development control, and sequential probes. It establishes neither a model/sampler/recorder mechanism nor a calibrated detector, so the current contribution is closer to a carefully scoped case-study audit than a decisive ICLR result.

paper_summary: The paper studies positionwise identity-lock profiles from an active-block recorder for blockwise diffusion-language-model decoding. It defines a min–max candidate-period selector and reports that its selected period follows configured block length for L16 and L64 main arms, a reused L32 development control, and sequential L24/L48 probes. It supplements this with same-profile rank-sum ordering, conditional permutation diagnostics, an exploratory DFT residual check, and a separate content-association analysis. The conclusion is deliberately recorder-relative and denies model, sampler, allocation, or universal-mechanism attribution.
strongest_verified_contribution: The strongest locally verifiable contribution is the finite-domain analysis itself: Eq. (2), the printed complete L16/L32/L64 candidate rows, and the boundary cardinalities are arithmetically consistent and yield P*=16, 32, and 64 respectively. All displayed schedules sum to 48 NFE; Table 14's per-decode row counts are conditionally consistent with recording the successively masked sets under the displayed divisible allocations. The discussion that midpoint medians with n=300 can be half-integral, while discreteness alone does not force a bootstrap point mass, is also correct.
strengths: The manuscript distinguishes demonstrated algebraic facts from source-reported empirical facts and repeatedly marks unavailable evidence as SR/CV.
The candidate domains are defined correctly on D_C={0,...,C-2}; Table 3's boundary/interior counts are correct: 15/240, 7/248, 3/252, 3/92, and 1/94.
All ordered schedules in Table 1 sum to 48 function evaluations: 8×4+8×2, 4×8+4×4, 2×16+2×8, 4×12, and 2×24.
The paper correctly explains that even-sample midpoint medians may be half-integral and that m(r), d(r), and sep(P) then lie on a half-step lattice without implying degenerate bootstrap uncertainty.
Bootstrap modal frequency, positivity frequency, percentile bands, permutation diagnostics, and rank-sum summaries are not misrepresented as independent calibrated hypothesis tests.
The conclusion respects the composite intervention and does not attribute the result to a model, sampler, allocation, or recorder mechanism.
Anonymity, the nine-page main-text limit, limitations, reproducibility boundaries, and AI-assisted-preparation disclosure are addressed.
questions: What is the exact type and unit of every step label in T_{i,r}: global function-evaluation index, block-local iteration, or position-observation ordinal? How do the reported P* values change under the other plausible coordinates?

How is x^f_{i,r} obtained when the active recorder contains only masked positions, and what exact rules handle empty observations, later re-entry, censoring, unresolved positions, and terminal-only units?
Are the same question identities aligned across every arm in the joint bootstrap, including the reused L32 pool, or are only row indices shared?
Can the complete six-candidate sep and rank-sum vectors, tie handling, and replicate-level outputs for L24/L48 be supplied?
Which content null was registered as primary: BIN8, emphasized in Section 2, or BIN16, described in Tables 11–12 as load-bearing? Was the granularity ladder fixed before inspecting outcomes?

issues.location: PDF p.3, Section 2, Eq. (1) and lines following it; PDF p.8, Section 4, “Event semantics”; PDF p.16, Appendix B, “Reported determinism claim”
issues.observed_evidence: The paper explicitly states that the package does not establish whether step labels are global, block-local, or position-observation ordinals and does not specify empty-set, absent-final-value, censoring, terminal, or unresolved-position handling. It consequently introduces unavailable position-specific analyzed sets A_r. These are cannot_verify gaps, not demonstrated evidence that the implementation is wrong.
issues.why_it_matters: The coordinate changes the meaning and comparability of ℓ across blocks. A global coordinate can introduce discontinuities through cumulative block progression, while a block-local coordinate interacts with the unequal ordered per-block allocations. Position-dependent exclusions can also make d(r) compare medians from changing decode cohorts. Thus the headline periodicity may depend on an undocumented measurement convention.
issues.required_fix: Provide a complete event-schema contract, pseudocode or executable implementation for Eq. (1), the exact step coordinate and final-value source, and explicit inclusion/censoring rules. Report positionwise analyzed counts and recompute all headline profiles under the declared semantics; either show robustness to plausible alternatives or narrow the claim to that exact coordinate and inclusion rule.
issues.verification_test: Construct hand-checkable traces covering token changes, permanent commitment, re-entry, empty observation, missing final value, and terminal-only cases. Confirm exact expected ℓ values, then rebuild m(r), d(r), every sep(P), and bootstrap readout from frozen events. Compare global and block-local coordinate outputs and verify that P*=L and candidate-32 signs do not arise solely from coordinate conversion or changing A_r.
issues.evidence_needed: Event-schema documentation, raw or reviewer-safe event streams, lock-time implementation, inclusion-count table by position and arm, and regenerated candidate vectors under the frozen convention.

issues.location: PDF pp.5–7, Tables 3–5 and Section 3.1; PDF p.8, “Probe auditability”; PDF p.12, Table 9
issues.observed_evidence: For L24 and L48, the paper supplies selected-candidate summaries and a few additional cells but omits the complete six-candidate separation vectors and all-candidate rank-sum scores. L24 has a marginal conditional margin p=0.071, and L48's selected separation is based on one boundary locus. The manuscript correctly labels the probe argmaxes source-reported/cannot_verify.
issues.why_it_matters: An argmax cannot be checked without every candidate score and the tie rule's actual application. These probes are the only non-power-of-two, non-nested extension, so their missing vectors materially weaken the evidence that period identity follows L beyond the three canvas-256 rows.
issues.required_fix: Supply the complete observed and bootstrap candidate vectors for both probes, candidate-set/tie metadata, rank-sum implementation and scores, and boundary-level values. Otherwise remove the probe argmaxes from the headline contribution and describe only the supplied candidate-32 cells as exploratory observations.
issues.verification_test: Recompute BP, IP, sep(P), P*, top-minus-second margins, bootstrap modal periods, positivity fractions, and rank-sum ordering for every P in {8,16,24,32,48,64}. Confirm that the published summaries and tie outcomes match and perform a leave-one-boundary analysis where cardinality permits.
issues.evidence_needed: Machine-readable L24/L48 profiles, all candidate scores, replicate outputs, analysis code, and provenance hashes.

issues.location: PDF p.4, Section 2, “Registration and two-layer reachability”; PDF p.8, Section 4, “Registration history”; PDF p.12, Appendix A.2, Table 8
issues.observed_evidence: The min–max estimator replaced a failed development score before the main runs, the L32 arm is reused from the development pool, and a model-intrinsic decision branch was withdrawn after main data. The timestamped registrations and diffs are absent, so the asserted chronology cannot be audited. The manuscript discloses these facts and limits its mechanistic conclusion.
issues.why_it_matters: Development-driven estimator selection and control reuse make the L32 recovery non-confirmatory, while the post-treatment branch withdrawal means the current scope cannot be treated as wholly prospective. The paper's repeated “registered” framing therefore carries less evidential weight than a frozen, auditable confirmatory protocol.
issues.required_fix: Provide blinded registration records with trusted timestamps and diffs, clearly label development-selected versus confirmatory components, and avoid counting the reused control as confirmation. A fresh frozen L32 control or an independent confirmatory arm would materially strengthen the claim.
issues.verification_test: Verify registration hashes and timestamps against execution times; reproduce the decision rule from the pre-run record without post-data edits; then apply it unchanged to a fresh control or independent arm and report all outcomes, including failures.
issues.evidence_needed: Timestamped registration artifacts and diffs, execution timestamps, frozen selector specification, and preferably a fresh confirmatory control.

issues.location: PDF pp.4–5, Section 2, “Selection stability” and Table 2; PDF p.3, Table 1
issues.observed_evidence: A common index draw is applied to two main arms, a reused development control, and sequential probes, but the exact item-pairing manifest and replicate indicators are absent. Table 1 does not establish that the reused control's row indices denote the same questions as all other arms.
issues.why_it_matters: Shared numeric indices are a meaningful paired cluster bootstrap only when they refer to matched sampling units. Otherwise the reported joint 2000/2000 relation has induced computational coupling without a justified paired-unit interpretation, although marginal arm summaries remain usable.
issues.required_fix: Document the arm-by-arm question-ID crosswalk and distinguish semantically paired arms from index-coupled but unmatched arms. Recompute the joint summary only over genuinely matched units or relabel it as a synchronized resampling diagnostic.
issues.verification_test: Hash and compare the ordered question manifests for all arms; verify each sampled index maps to the same question where pairing is claimed; reproduce the 2000 joint indicators from the saved draw indices.
issues.evidence_needed: Reviewer-safe question-pairing manifest, bootstrap draw indices, and replicate-level P* indicators.

issues.location: PDF pp.3–4, Section 2, “Setup and protocol” and “Separately conditioned content analysis”; PDF pp.14–15, Tables 11–12
issues.observed_evidence: Section 2 foregrounds BIN8 as the explicit restricted content null, but Table 11 uses BIN16 for the principal content-layer readout and calls it load-bearing; BIN8 appears as a nuisance-refit sensitivity. The package does not clarify which granularity was prospectively primary or how the ladder was selected.
issues.why_it_matters: Null granularity strongly changes q95, reaching a zero-power point mass at BIN32. Without a frozen primary choice, the positive supporting content claim is vulnerable to outcome-dependent granularity selection even though it is not part of the headline cross-length result.
issues.required_fix: State the registered primary granularity and selection rule, reconcile Section 2 with Tables 11–12, and label the ladder exploratory if it was chosen post hoc. Supply outcomes for every registered granularity and any multiplicity treatment.
issues.verification_test: Compare the frozen protocol with the implemented K ladder; rerun every K using identical units and replicates; verify reported q95 values and that the content conclusion follows the prespecified rule rather than a favorable intermediate bin count.
issues.evidence_needed: Registration for the content null, permutation code, full replicate distributions, and fixed-fit/refit nuisance specifications.

ethics_concerns: No direct human-subject, privacy, or deployment-harm concern is apparent from the reviewer-safe snapshot. The manuscript discloses AI-assisted editing and an image-generated qualitative figure; missing prompt/model provenance is a transparency limitation but does not affect quantitative evidence because Figure 1 is explicitly non-evidentiary.
llm_usage_disclosure: This review was produced by A31-R01-T, a fresh isolated AI subagent, for internal pre-submission quality control. It used only the frozen PDF, manifest, rubric, reviewer instructions, reviewer-safe evidence summaries, citation lock, and source-hash record supplied inside the snapshot; it did not access the internet, parent directories, repository history, prior reviews, author notes, or revision records.
evidence_that_would_raise_score: A frozen event-time and missingness contract plus executable lock-time code and reviewer-safe events that reproduce every profile, separation, and uncertainty summary.
Complete L24/L48 separation and rank-sum candidate vectors demonstrating the reported argmaxes, with additional boundary loci for L48 or a narrower claim.
Auditable pre-run registrations and a fresh confirmatory control or independent arm evaluated without changing the selector.
A dual-recorder comparison on identical trajectories or a partition-by-allocation factorial that separates recorder-window, partition, and allocation effects.
A prespecified, arm-level structured null with family-wise calibration for the full candidate-selection procedure.
Independent replication across another checkpoint/model family, task, schedule, or recorder while preserving exact event semantics.
evidence_that_would_lower_score: Evidence that global versus block-local step coordinates change P*, candidate-32 signs, or the apparent boundary structure.
Positionwise exclusion counts aligned with block boundaries or allocation transitions strongly enough to explain d(r).
Complete probe vectors showing that an omitted candidate ties or exceeds L under the registered tie rule.
A question manifest showing that supposedly paired arm indices refer to different sampling units.
Timestamped records showing that the selector, candidate grid, probe plan, or content-null granularity was altered after inspecting the corresponding outcomes.
Recomputed structured-null results showing high wrong-candidate selection or failure of the reported margins.
review_limitations: All empirical results are explicitly source-reported/cannot_verify because events, programs, machine-readable results, private checkpoint, full registrations, and complete probe vectors are absent.
Novelty assessment is limited to the reviewer-safe partial citation audit; no internet or bibliography-wide verification was performed.
The assessment verifies internal arithmetic and logic from the full 17-page PDF but cannot reproduce numerical experiments from the supplied snapshot.
